clue.text: Endless kisses give you spots

annotationWithheld.why: Endless kisses give you spots (6): kisses gives PECKS, but no reading of 'Endless' supplies the leading S of SPECKS

clue.text: Even a moment before, you are said to be my lover

parts.note: par means level or even, as in 'on a par'
mo is short for a moment, as in 'wait a mo'

indicators.note: said tells us the words you are are spoken, giving the letter sounds

parts.note: spoken quickly 'you are' sounds like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: A suitor insists, just before the moment of truth, that their sweetheart is spoken for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes 'you are' into the two letters that sound like it, U and R, as in text-speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit or secret lover, so 'my lover' fits a possessive phrase.

clue.text: Rode erect — and fell!

indicators.note: fell, read as a verb of collapse, tells us the letters of the two words tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider sat bolt upright on the horse and then took a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' rearranges ERECT and AND; the dash and exclamation make it look like a story of a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To canter is to ride at a gait between trot and gallop, so the past tense matches rode.

clue.text: Settle down — crazy to get up — one lies around

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word is written upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of lies are scattered about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frantic is told to calm down while another person lazes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns the word for crazy upwards in this down entry; 'around' scrambles the letters of the clue word lies rather than wrapping anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To stabilise is to make or become steady, the sense of settling down after disturbance.

clue.text: Chamber, when full, had this to report

definitions.text: Chamber, when full, had this to report

parts.words: Chamber, when full, had this to report
parts.note: a gun's chamber, once loaded, has a round sitting inside it; read the other way it is a short news report

explanation.surface: A parliamentary chamber, packed to capacity, issued a news statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' suggests parliament, but it is the chamber of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news report, the thing a full chamber had to announce.

clue.text: Snap, when told what to do with the jelly babies?

definitions.text: when told what to do with the jelly babies?

explanation.surface: A child is snapped at when asked how to eat the sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Jelly babies are British gummy sweets shaped like little people, which many eat head first.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak to someone angrily and sharply is an idiom for snapping; literally it is how one eats the sweets, decapitating them.

clue.text: Leaves permit with unions, eager to start

parts.note: to let is to permit
TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the British federation of trade unions

indicators.note: to start points to the opening letter of the word eager

explanation.surface: Bosses allow something while unions are keen to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: TUC, the Trades Union Congress, is Britain's umbrella body for trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettuce is a salad plant eaten for its leaves.

clue.text: Value certain to support rate renegotiation

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after
renegotiation suggests the terms of the word rate are reworked into a new order

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone is confident of backing a renegotiated rate of pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renegotiation' rearranges RATE into TREA; 'to support' puts SURE beneath it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to value it highly.

clue.text: In 10 letters, the most stylish

indicators.note: letters invites us to treat the words as a set of letters to be reshuffled

parts.note: 10 refers to the answer to 10 across, attest

explanation.surface: Among ten letters lies the most fashionable choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 refers to 10 across, ATTEST; 'letters' says IN and ATTEST are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and stylish, so its superlative is the most stylish.

clue.text: Deal! Managed to finish courses in diplomacy

indicators.note: in shows the inner pieces are placed inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: to finish points to the closing letter of the word courses

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike a bargain after completing courses in diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes 'Deal!' an imperative, matching the verb in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to conduct or carry out business, so it means to deal.

clue.text: Witness attending trial

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone gives evidence while present at a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify something is true.

clue.text: Condition in which I am favourite before I leave

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A child complains of being the favourite until departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious skin infection, a medical condition.

clue.text: Think aloud and flit inside for breakfast

indicators.note: aloud says the word for think is to be spoken, and only its sound kept

parts.note: to muse is to think or ponder

indicators.note: inside points to the inner letters of the word flit

explanation.surface: Someone ponders out loud before dashing off for the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aloud' keeps the sound of MUSE, the 'mews' heard in the answer; 'inside' takes LI from FLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and fruit eaten at the morning meal.

clue.text: Study in English sin providing proof

indicators.note: in shows the study word is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: vice is a sin
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A study of English wrongdoing supplies proof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' is only a link: the wordplay provides the definition 'proof'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is information that establishes a fact, a synonym of proof.

clue.text: Frank worried the applicant

parts.note: candid means frank and open
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: An honest person was troubled by the job seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, but it is the adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is a person who applies for a job or post.

clue.text: Dry run — help is outside

indicators.note: is outside says the help word wraps round the run letter

parts.note: aid is help
R is the abbreviation for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A rehearsal goes ahead while assistance waits outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means parched, lacking moisture.

clue.text: A way over his puzzled surprise

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
on can mean over, as in on top of

indicators.note: puzzled suggests the letters of his are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: A path across his estate leaves him baffled and surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze or greatly surprise.

clue.text: Gut feeling that's vague, when the di goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing tells us the letters di vanish from the longer word

parts.note: indistinct means vague or blurred

explanation.surface: A hunch that is hazy, appearing when Princess Di has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Di' looks like the princess, but it is just the two letters taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is an innate, unreasoned urge, what we call a gut feeling.

clue.text: Group caught in position

indicators.note: in says the caught letter is placed inside

parts.note: to set is to position or place
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A gang is captured in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a group with distinctive religious or political beliefs.

clue.text: Critical of little girl in voice

indicators.note: in says the girl's name is placed inside

parts.note: to voice a tune is to sing
Cath is a short form of the girl's name Catherine

explanation.surface: Disapproving remarks about a small girl's singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing means severely critical or scornful.

clue.text: Horse box enthusiast

parts.note: a chest is a large box
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a health nut

explanation.surface: A fan of horses is given a box for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a horse of reddish-brown colour.

clue.text: Chance I'm prepared to take for service-man

indicators.note: prepared hints the letters are made ready by being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to take a risk for a serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service-man' suggests a soldier, but it is someone who services cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic services and repairs vehicles and machines, the hyphen splitting service-man for that sense.

clue.text: Remain confused by origin of tall tower

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of remain are mixed up
origin of points to the opening letter of the word tall

explanation.surface: Puzzled, someone stays by the base of a high tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is a slender tower of a mosque.

clue.text: Pleasure trip that's revealing

explanation.surface: An excursion that exposes something.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is an excursion for fun; outing someone is exposing their secret, such as their sexuality.

clue.text: By which one proves cat's diet is poor?

indicators.note: is poor suggests the letters of the two words are in bad shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: How to show that a pet's food is substandard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is poor' rearranges CATS and DIET; the acid test was originally a test for gold using nitric acid.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial of worth is called an acid test, a way of proving something.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge some topless Italian ladies

indicators.note: topless means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: signore is the plural of signora, Italian for lady

explanation.surface: Snubbing some Italian women sunbathing without tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter S from SIGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them deliberately.

clue.text: Limits put on Romeo's final speeches

indicators.note: put on means placed before, in front of the next piece
final points to the closing letter of the word Romeo

parts.note: rations are fixed allowances, limits

explanation.surface: Restrictions placed on Romeo's last addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Orations are formal public addresses.

clue.text: Warm material with the quality of being exciting

definitions.text: with the quality of being exciting

parts.note: hot is warm in a stronger degree
stuff is material, cloth

explanation.surface: Cosy fabric that has a thrilling appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something or someone described in slang as thrilling or sexy is said to be red-hot.

clue.text: Crew start to hurry just a fraction

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word hurry

explanation.surface: A rowing team begins to speed up only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' is an eight, a racing boat with eight rowers.
explanation.definitionFit: One eighth is a fraction, one part in eight.
